audit_comment: The damage-from-falling slice pins Table 17 (the six fall-distance bands x the band-minimum distances and the cumulative damage dice) with the falling-vs-tumbling prose (the vertical-drop definition, the 1d6-cumulative-per-10-feet basis, the recurring-impact rule on severe slopes, the smooth/slippery abrasion note and the 1000 and 600-800 feet-per-round rates) (rules/wsgfall.h, prefix wdf); census 361 -> 362.

banner.title: The WSG DAMAGE FROM FALLING, R437: Table 17 (the damage from free fall or severe slope - the six fall-distance bands: 10 feet 1d6, 11-20 feet 3d6, 21-30 feet 6d6, 31-40 feet 10d6, 41-50 feet 15d6 and 51 feet or more 20d6, the maximum) with the prose rules: falling is distinguished from tumbling (the former much more liable to cause serious injury or death, the latter able in the least perilous circumstances to result in nothing more than a minor inconvenience; tumbling down a moderate or gentle slope is Table 18, the next round), falling describes a vertical drop (the character releases his hold on a cliff face or a severe slope and plummets until hitting a surface that stops the fall), the damage is 1d6 cumulative for each 10 feet fallen, the figures apply to free fall and to tumbling down a severe slope (the recurring impact with the slope plus the stop at the end), on a smooth and/or slippery slope the abrasion damage on the way down is not a great factor but the greater velocity makes the end result essentially the same as a rough slope at a slower speed, and an unimpeded fall covers 1000 feet per round in free fall or 600-800 feet per round down a severe slope depending on the texture and degree of slipperiness - the round continues the movement-across-special-terrain section. Census 361 -> 362.

banner.sentinel: The Table 17 figures are cumulative damage dice by the fall-distance band - 1d6 for each 10 feet fallen, capped at the 20d6 maximum in the 51-feet-or-more band. They apply to free fall and to tumbling down a severe slope.

consts.name: wdfFallBandCount
consts.comment: The Table 17 damage-band count (10, 11-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-50 and 51-or-more feet).

consts.name: wdfFreeFallRate
consts.comment: A character whose fall is not impeded or stopped falls 1000 feet per round in free fall.

consts.name: wdfSevereRateMin
consts.comment: An unimpeded fall down a severe slope covers at least 600 feet per round.

consts.name: wdfSevereRateMax
consts.comment: An unimpeded fall down a severe slope covers at most 800 feet per round, depending on the texture and degree of slipperiness of the slope.

consts.name: wdfMaxFallDice
consts.comment: The 51-feet-or-more band damage is 20d6 - the maximum.

bools.name: wdfFallingVsTumbling
bools.comment: A distinction is made between falling and tumbling - the former is much more liable to cause serious injury or death, while the latter can in the least perilous circumstances result in nothing more than a minor inconvenience.

bools.name: wdfFallingIsVerticalDrop
bools.comment: Falling describes a vertical drop: the character releases his hold on a cliff face or a severe slope and plummets down until hitting a surface that stops the fall.

bools.name: wdfDiceCumulativePer10Ft
bools.comment: A character takes damage from a fall at the rate of 1d6 cumulative for each 10 feet fallen.

bools.name: wdfAppliesFreeFallOrSevere
bools.comment: The Table 17 damage figures apply whether the character is in free fall or tumbling down a severe slope.

bools.name: wdfSevereTumbleRecurringImpact
bools.comment: Tumbling down a severe slope, the character is assumed to take some damage from recurring impact with the slope itself, in addition to being hurt when he comes to a stop at the end of the fall.

bools.name: wdfSmoothSlipperyAbrasionNote
bools.comment: On a smooth and/or slippery severe slope, abrasion damage on the way down is not a great factor - but the body reaches a greater velocity, so the end result is essentially the same as tumbling down a rough slope at a slower speed.

bools.name: wdfTumbleModerateGentleNext
bools.comment: Tumbling - handled by Table 18 - is what happens to a character who slips and leaves his feet, or releases his handholds and footholds, and tumbles down a moderate or gentle slope; it is pinned by the next round.
